recurring_scale_anchors: Canvas 304×192; keep instrument silhouettes large and immediately recognizable.
Distinguish close instrument families by their body, bell, keys, strings, slide or playing posture.
No lettering, readable titles, numbers, logos, brands or publisher marks; musical note marks may be simple geometric cues.
When a music word has another dictionary meaning, use the explicit Music chapter group and the surrounding terms to choose the musical sense.
Keep performance settings varied so a store, studio, rehearsal, concert and street performance are not interchangeable.

polysemy_resolution_table.cello: Large bowed string instrument with a rounded wooden body, long neck, bow and floor endpin; much larger than a violin.
polysemy_resolution_table.clarinet: Straight dark woodwind with a mouthpiece, silver keys and a flared bell; distinguish it from the curved saxophone.
polysemy_resolution_table.drum / drums: A small drum kit with bass drum, snare, toms, cymbals and sticks; show the plural set rather than one hand drum.
polysemy_resolution_table.electric guitar: Solid-body guitar with pickups, bridge controls and an amp cable; distinct from the hollow acoustic guitar.
polysemy_resolution_table.flute: Silver transverse flute held horizontally, with lip plate, keys and a short foot joint.
polysemy_resolution_table.guitar: Acoustic wooden guitar with a hollow body and visible sound hole; distinct from the electric guitar.
polysemy_resolution_table.harmonica: Small handheld mouth organ with a row of air holes, held to a player’s mouth.
polysemy_resolution_table.keyboard: A musical keyboard with piano-style black and white keys, not a computer or typewriter keyboard.
polysemy_resolution_table.saxophone: Curved brass-colored single-reed woodwind with a neck, keys and broad flared bell; distinct from the straight clarinet.
polysemy_resolution_table.tambourine: Handheld shallow frame drum with paired metal jingles around its rim.
polysemy_resolution_table.trombone: Brass instrument with a long moving slide and broad bell; make its slide prominent.
polysemy_resolution_table.trumpet: Compact brass instrument with three valves and a flared bell; distinct from the trombone slide.
polysemy_resolution_table.violin: Small bowed string instrument with chin rest, four strings, bridge and bow; distinct from the larger cello.
polysemy_resolution_table.instrument: A group of clearly recognizable musical instruments, not precision tools or gauges; adapt the existing music collage.
polysemy_resolution_table.piano: Full-size acoustic piano with broad keyboard and raised lid or visible upright case; distinct from a portable keyboard.
polysemy_resolution_table.band: A small musical ensemble performing together, not a belt, strap or barrel hoop.
polysemy_resolution_table.choir: Several singers standing together and singing in harmony, not a single vocalist.
polysemy_resolution_table.composer: A person creating a piece of music at a desk with score sheets and a composing gesture.
polysemy_resolution_table.conductor: A person leading an ensemble with a baton and clear conducting gesture, not a generic guide.
polysemy_resolution_table.group: A small ensemble of musicians playing together; show several people and instruments.
polysemy_resolution_table.guitar player: A musician visibly playing a guitar, with hands on strings and fretboard; person is the focus.
polysemy_resolution_table.orchestra: Large seated ensemble with string, wind and brass sections led by a conductor; distinct from a small band.
polysemy_resolution_table.singer: One vocalist singing, with microphone and breath or note cues; distinct from a choir.
polysemy_resolution_table.solo: One musician alone in a clear spotlight, performing an instrumental or vocal solo.
polysemy_resolution_table.musician: A working music maker with an instrument and performance or practice cues; broad profession, not one instrument.
polysemy_resolution_table.classical: Classical music shown by a small string ensemble or formal score, not an ancient object.
polysemy_resolution_table.country: Country music as a genre, suggested by acoustic guitar, fiddle or banjo and a live country-stage setting; not a nation or map.
polysemy_resolution_table.hip-hop: Hip-hop music culture with a DJ turntable, MC microphone and rhythmic movement; avoid relying on clothing stereotypes.
polysemy_resolution_table.jazz: Jazz ensemble with improvising players such as saxophone, bass and piano in a small club setting.
polysemy_resolution_table.latin: Latin music genre shown through percussion, guitar and dancing; not the Latin language or a map.
polysemy_resolution_table.opera: Opera performance on a theater stage with a dramatic singer, curtain and orchestral accompaniment.
polysemy_resolution_table.pop: Pop music performance with a singer, bright stage and broad audience; not the verb meaning to burst.
polysemy_resolution_table.rap: A solo MC delivering rhythmic vocals into a microphone over a beat; distinguish the vocal style from a hip-hop DJ scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.rock (music): Rock music performed by a guitar-driven band with drums and stage amplifiers; not a stone.
polysemy_resolution_table.soul: Soul music as an expressive vocal genre, shown by a lead singer with warm band or choir accompaniment; not a spirit.
polysemy_resolution_table.album: A music album shown as a record sleeve or LP collection, not a photo album.
polysemy_resolution_table.lyrics: The words sung in a song, shown by a vocalist and a lyric sheet with music cues but no readable writing.
polysemy_resolution_table.music: Music as an audible art, shown by instruments and flowing sound marks; avoid a single genre.
polysemy_resolution_table.music store: A retail shop displaying records, headphones and instruments for sale; distinct from a bookstore or library.
polysemy_resolution_table.microphone: A standalone vocal microphone with grille, stand and cable; no performer needed.
polysemy_resolution_table.beat: A regular pulse in music, shown by a drummer striking a drum and evenly spaced sound pulses.
polysemy_resolution_table.headphones: Over-ear headphones with padded ear cups and headband, shown as listening equipment.
polysemy_resolution_table.melody: A tuneful sequence of notes, represented by a flowing line of sound from an instrument.
polysemy_resolution_table.playlist: An ordered selection of music tracks shown as a device screen with several simple play markers, without text or logos.
polysemy_resolution_table.rhythm: A repeated pattern of long and short musical beats, shown by percussion and repeated sound marks; distinct from one steady beat.
polysemy_resolution_table.song: A musical composition with a vocalist or singing cue and accompanying notes; distinct from lyrics alone.
polysemy_resolution_table.streaming: Music arriving wirelessly over a network to a listening device; show a phone, sound waves and connection arcs without a platform logo.
polysemy_resolution_table.busk: A musician performing outdoors for passersby with an open instrument case for tips.
polysemy_resolution_table.compose: Create or arrange a piece of music at a score desk; show musical notes and a composing hand, not general organization.
polysemy_resolution_table.concert: A public live music event with stage performers and an audience.
polysemy_resolution_table.conduct: Lead musicians by directing an orchestra with a baton; use the music-group sense despite the broad Japanese gloss.
polysemy_resolution_table.dance: A person moving to music with clear full-body steps and sound cues.
polysemy_resolution_table.festival: Outdoor music festival with a stage, crowd, instruments and celebratory bunting; keep music central.
polysemy_resolution_table.listen: Attend carefully to live music, with a listener leaning toward a nearby performer; distinct from the headphone object.
polysemy_resolution_table.perform: Present music before an audience, showing an active musician onstage; use the performance sense in this chapter.
polysemy_resolution_table.play the trumpet: A musician blowing a trumpet with fingers on its valves; distinct from the standalone trumpet object.
polysemy_resolution_table.practice: A musician repeatedly working on an instrument in a quiet room, with a metronome or marked rehearsal pattern.
polysemy_resolution_table.record: Capture a musical performance in a recording studio with microphone, headphones and a sound waveform.
polysemy_resolution_table.rehearse: A group of musicians practicing together before a performance, distinct from the public concert.
polysemy_resolution_table.sing: One person producing a sung vocal line, with open mouth and sound notes; distinct from singer as a profession.

glossary_context_notes: Use the music genre sense for country, Latin, pop, rap, rock and soul because they appear under Styles and genres.
Use the musical group sense for band, and the orchestra-leading sense for conduct; the Japanese glosses list other general senses.
Use the chapter context for album, perform and compose while keeping the visual meaning clearly music-related.
Reviewed the generic concert and turntable candidates against the five genre terms; neither carries enough style-specific cues, so all five genre cards were authored for their own musical contexts.
Reviewed generic singer, band, concert and choir candidates against the five genres; they remain reserved for their exact senses because each genre needs distinct stage, instrumental or vocal cues.

The album entry follows the Music group rather than the Japanese photo/stamp-album gloss; it shows an LP release. Adapted the clear existing turntable scene for music and removed an unrelated plus mark; authored separate lyrics, music-store and microphone scenes.

No direct beat, melody, playlist or rhythm candidates were found. Reviewed headphone-bearing listening and podcast scenes; the person or recording setup dominated, so the object entry uses a clear standalone over-ear pair. Beat is one steady pulse; rhythm uses a repeated alternating pattern; melody is a flowing pitched phrase.

Adapted the strong connected-device streaming scene from video to music playback; kept the direct concert scene after adding a crop-safe frame. Rejected the river for streaming, the composer profession image for the compose verb, and the generic guitarist/stage scenes for busking; authored a street scene with an open tip case.

Adapted the direct rhythmic-dance illustration for this music group. Rejected the conductor-role image as a duplicate for conduct, headphone scenes for live listening, the concert event image for perform, and the indoor concert for festival; created distinct action and outdoor-event scenes.
Adapted the music-practice violinist from Lesson 59 for the generic music practice verb; rejected the Lesson 60 running workout because it is sports practice.
Adapted the Lesson 58 podcast recording setup for record in the music sense, adding musical cues; it shows recording equipment and a waveform rather than a person speaking into a podcast.
Rejected the standalone Lesson 64 trumpet object for play the trumpet because it has no player or playing action; scaled the new musician-and-trumpet scene to keep the performer visually dominant.

Rejected the generic Lesson 64 group image for rehearse because it duplicates group and lacks pre-performance cues; authored a small ensemble with scores and a metronome. Sing is a single human vocal action, distinct from the choir and bird candidates.
